summary: Added plugins/builtin/world-look.js — the "World Look" plugin, the only file I touched. On level:loaded it reads the level's optional "world" block and drives the four renderer setters: setSky(colour|null), setFog(density, colour), setAmbient(intensity, colour), setSun([dx,dy,dz], intensity, colour). Every call is guarded on context.renderer and on the setter existing, so a headless world loads, applies nothing and still reports the numbers it would have used. Values are read in loose forms (a bare number, a bare colour, a pair, or the full object) and each reader returns only what was actually stated, so defaults sit underneath and a single-field change never resets its neighbours. "skyTexture" adds an inverted THREE.SphereGeometry to context.renderer.scene — BackSide, fog:false, depthTest/depthWrite off, renderOrder -1000, radius 100 m, re-centred on context.view every frame by a phase:'frame' system, so it never occludes and the player can never reach it. three and engine/ui.js (for assetURL) are dynamically imported inside that browser-only path, so headless never loads them. Two commands: world.look reports sky, skyTexture, sky-box status, fog (with the distance at which it half washes out), ambient, sun, what the level declared, what world.set changed this session, and notes explaining anything suspicious — including "nothing is drawing this world"; world.set changes one key at runtime (or a whole block as one object) without writing to disk, and world.set '["fog"]' undoes the change back to what the level declared.
notes:
IMPORTANT, not caused by this work: `node bin/engine.mjs --headless run tests.run` currently reports 6 passed / 1 failed. The failure is project/tests/first-person-camera.js (recoil kick not decaying, crouch not easing) — another agent's in-flight test against their own camera plugin. I verified it by moving plugins/builtin/world-look.js out of the tree and re-running: identical failure, identical assertions. The five original tests plus the new mouse-look test all pass, and `node bin/engine.mjs check` reports {"ok":true,"problems":[]}.

Numbers other agents may care about:
- DEFAULT_FOG_DENSITY is 0.014, not the 0.02 in the contract's example. FogExp2 washes out by 1-exp(-(density*metres)^2), so 0.014 leaves a wall 40 m away (about long A) a quarter gone, half at 60 m, nine tenths by 100 m. A level that writes its own density is honoured exactly; 0.014 only fills in for "fog": true or a colour-only fog. 0.02 is perfectly usable — it just half-washes at 42 m.
- With no "world" block a level gets sky null, fog off, and lit defaults (ambient 0.55 #93a7c4, sun [-0.4,-1,-0.3] 0.9 #fff2d8). Lights are applied even when undeclared so a level switch cannot leak the previous level's sun and a 3D level can never be black; unlit sprite materials ignore them, so the 2D path is unchanged. Sky and fog are reset to null/0 when undeclared, for the same anti-leak reason — a 2D level after a 3D one gets its transparent background back.
- The plugin contributes context.worldLook = { declared, overrides, resolved, skyMesh, skyStatus, apply(), set(key, value), report() } if any other plugin wants to fade the sky or dim the light at runtime. Nothing in the six-way contract depends on it.
- If engine/render.js lands without one of the four setters, the browser console gets one [World Look] line naming the missing method and the rest still apply; it never throws inside level:loaded.
- The sky box is not rebuilt when the same texture is reloaded, and the frame system re-adds it if something clears the scene, so a renderer rewrite cannot make the sky silently vanish.
- Level authors: "world": { "sky": "#6d7f96", "skyTexture": "counter-strike/sky.png", "fog": [0.014, "#8a94a3"], "ambient": {...}, "sun": {...} }. skyTexture is one panorama image mapped to a sphere (not six cube faces); a bare name resolves under project/assets/, a name with a slash resolves under project/.
- CLI: values must arrive as one JSON argument — `run world.set '["fog", 0.02]'`. `run world.set fog 0.02` drops the value in bin/engine.mjs, so the command detects that shape and throws with the working syntax instead of quietly setting nothing.

summary: Built the "Mouse Look" plugin (needs: ["Keyboard Input"]) and its test. It extends the existing input surface rather than replacing it: context.input.look() drains a radian accumulator, context.input.lookBy(yaw, pitch) fills the same one by hand, context.input.mouseWheel() drains wheel counts, context.input.locked is a plain boolean, and context.input.sensitivity is a validated accessor defaulting to 2.5 with radians-per-count = sensitivity * 0.022 * PI / 180. It binds the whole first-person action set (forward/back/strafeLeft/strafeRight/jump/crouch/walk/attack/attack2/reload/use/buy/drop/score/inspect/slot1..slot5), routes Mouse0/Mouse1 through the keyboard plugin's press/release so held("attack") works unchanged, captures the pointer on a canvas click while play mode is running, releases it on play:stopped, suppresses the context menu, and reports a refused pointer lock by name on the console with a [mouse-look] prefix and what to do about it. Everything DOM-shaped lives behind a shell:ready listener and a document guard, so the plugin is inert but fully functional headless. Adds one command, mouse.sensitivity, which reads with no argument and sets with a number (exit 1 on a bad value).
notes:
DELIBERATE DEVIATION — jump is now ["Space", "ArrowUp"], with KeyW removed. KeyW became `forward`, and jump still held it from the platformer, so a first-person player holding forward would have bunny-hopped continuously. Space (what the demo and project/tests/jump.js press, via codes('jump')[0]) and ArrowUp are untouched, so nothing the platformer relies on changed. left/right/up/down/fire are byte-for-byte as they were, and my test asserts all six tables so a later change reports itself.

HOW A TEST REACHES THE LIVE INPUT — the test runner hands a test only the `test` object, never `context`, so there is no supported way for project/tests/*.js to read anything a plugin contributed. plugins/builtin/mouse-look.js therefore publishes `export const mouseLook = { input: null }`, set in onLoad, and the test imports it by relative path. A plugin module is one instance in node and in the browser alike (node resolves the test's ../../plugins/... to the same file URL findPlugins imported; Vite serves the same /plugins/builtin/ URL the glob uses). Worth noting this is a converged convention, not just my choice: the camera agent independently exported `runningCamera()` from camera.js for exactly the same reason, and project/tests/first-person-camera.js imports it the same way. The underlying engine gap — a test cannot see `context` — is a real painpoint. I did NOT append it to painpoints.jsonl, because six agents appending to one file concurrently would interleave; someone should record it after the fan-out lands.

ALSO EXPORTED, ON PURPOSE: `radiansPerCount(sensitivity)` and `lookFromMouse(movementX, movementY, sensitivity)`. The second is pure so the two signs everyone notices are testable with no mouse — it returns { yaw: -movementX * radians, pitch: -movementY * radians }, i.e. mouse right lowers yaw (turns right, since positive yaw about +Y turns left) and mouse down lowers pitch. The mousemove handler calls it and then lookBy, so the mouse takes the same route a test and a bot take; there is no second input path.

BEHAVIOUR OTHER AGENTS SHOULD KNOW:
- Mouse buttons only register while the pointer is captured. The click that takes the lock is swallowed on purpose ("give me the mouse", not a shot). Headless and tests are unaffected — they call press("Mouse0") directly.
- The look accumulator is cleared on both play:started and play:stopped, so a stale half-turn cannot whip the view on the first step. A test that arranges aim then simulates is unaffected (simulate emits neither).
- The wheel accumulates raw deltaY, only while locked, so the editor's own wheel gestures never reach weapon switching.
- Tab and Space get preventDefault only while locked (focus-stealing and page scroll); the editor keeps both while editing.
- On unlock, Mouse0/Mouse1 are released — Escape gives the pointer back without a mouseup, and the symptom would be a weapon firing forever.
- input.sensitivity refuses a non-finite or negative value, reports it as [mouse-look], and keeps the old value; `run mouse.sensitivity abc` also exits 1.

I touched no file other than the two I own; I did not run npm test or start a server.

summary: Extended the Game Camera plugin with a first-person camera alongside the existing 2D follow, and added project/tests/first-person-camera.js to prove it. The fixed system now branches on context.view.mode: 'first-person' reads context.input.look() once per step into view.yaw/view.pitch (pitch clamped to plus or minus 89 degrees, yaw wrapped into plus or minus PI), puts the eye at the followed body's feet plus an eased eye height, and applies recoil and shake as angular offsets. The 2D branch is byte-for-byte the code that was there before — lerp, lookAhead, offsetY, bounds and positional shake are untouched. context.camera gained aim(), punch(pitchRadians, yawRadians), forward() and right(); play:started now saves and play:stopped now restores x, y, z, zoom, mode, yaw, pitch and fov together; camera.state reports the mode, angles, fov, aim, eye position and current eye height.
notes:
ANGLE CONVENTION (written into the file header, and the thing to check first if anything shoots backwards): Y up, YXZ order, yaw about +Y, pitch about +X, yaw 0 / pitch 0 faces -Z, positive yaw turns LEFT, positive pitch looks UP.
  forward = ( -sin(yaw)*cos(pitch),  sin(pitch),  -cos(yaw)*cos(pitch) )
  right   = (  cos(yaw),             0,           -sin(yaw)            )
right is forward x up, so the basis is right-handed the same way Three.js is. Verified numerically end to end.

WHAT THE MOVEMENT AGENT MUST DO: crouch is read as the plain entity field `entity.crouched === true` (with `entity.properties.crouched` accepted as well). Nothing else tells the camera to duck. Whoever writes player movement has to set that field or the eye stays at standing height. This follows the engine's rule that two plugins which must agree do it through plain fields on the entity.

RECOIL MODEL: view.yaw / view.pitch carry the aim PLUS whatever punch and shake are adding this instant; the system subtracts last step's offset before integrating the mouse, so the kick cannot drift the aim (verified: after a shake decays the view returns to the base angle exactly). camera.aim() = aim + punch and deliberately EXCLUDES shake — a screen effect must not decide where a bullet goes. forward() and right() both go through aim(). Punch decays exponentially with a 0.09 s time constant and snaps to exactly zero below 1e-5 rad.

MODE IS DECIDED BY context.view.mode, NOT by the level rule. The rule only sets the mode when play starts (the kernel's loadLevel already applies it in edit mode). That is what lets a test or another plugin switch cameras.

TEST SEAM: a test file receives only the `test` object, so there was no way for one to read context.view. plugins/builtin/camera.js now exports `runningCamera()` returning { camera, context } — a plugin module is a singleton in node and in the browser alike, so `import { runningCamera } from '../../plugins/builtin/camera.js'` inside project/tests reaches the live object. If a future agent adds `test.context` or `test.view` to plugins/builtin/tests.js, this export becomes redundant and the test should move onto it. The test also stands in for context.input.look()/lookBy() if Mouse Look is absent and notes which path it took; Mouse Look now exists, so it drives the real accumulator.

TWO SMALL FIXES BEYOND THE BRIEF, both inside camera.js: (1) the level:loaded handler used to clear cam.target AFTER awaiting the file read, so a run that pressed play during that read had its follow wiped — the reset is now synchronous and the rule applies itself late if play got there first, guarded by a level-name token so a stale read cannot overwrite a newer level. (2) camera.state is now async and awaits cam.ruleRead; it used to report `rule: {}` on a fresh headless boot, which reads as "the level declared no camera" rather than "the read has not landed".

ORDERING: plugins load by sorted filename, so the camera's fixed system runs before Physics 2D and Physics 3D. The eye therefore follows the body's position at the start of the step — one fixed step of lag. I deliberately did NOT add `needs: ['Physics 3D']` to reorder it, because that would also change the 2D camera's timing and the brief says the 2D path must behave exactly as it does now. If the lag is ever visible, that is the one-line fix, but it needs the 2D tests re-checked.

CONSTANTS, all named at the top of camera.js: eye 1.62 standing / 0.91 crouched (overridable per level as eyeHeight / crouchEyeHeight), eye ease 0.05 s time constant (about 0.15 s to arrive), recoil decay 0.09 s, bob 0.035 m at 12 rad/s scaled by speed over 6.35 m/s and only while grounded, landing dip up to 0.12 m proportional to impact speed with a 0.09 s decay, shake 0.08 rad per unit.

summary: Turned engine/render.js into a renderer that draws both a 2D sprite scene and a 3D first-person scene from one GL context, one scene graph and one texture cache. Added: a PerspectiveCamera built alongside the existing OrthographicCamera and selected by view.mode (position from view.x/y/z, rotation order YXZ, yaw/pitch/fov from view, aspect from the viewport, near 0.05, far 400); box and quad geometry for entities carrying `mesh`, cached by dimensions and with those dimensions inside the rebuild key so an inspector edit shows up without a reload; MeshLambertMaterial (MeshBasicMaterial when `unlit`), opaque, depth-writing, depth-testing, back-face culled, while sprites keep painter ordering in ortho and start testing depth whenever the mode is not ortho; a second `world` reading of texture() with LinearMipmapLinearFilter, generated mipmaps, RepeatWrapping and maximum anisotropy, cached separately from the `sprite` reading so the same file can be both; per-entity texture clones so two walls tiling one file differently never share a texture; tint (declared hex multiplied into the texture, or the stable per-type colour when there is no texture); an AmbientLight and DirectionalLight created with dust2 defaults plus the four contract setters setSky/setFog/setAmbient/setSun; and perspective routing for pick(), toScreen() and toWorld() through a THREE.Raycaster and camera.project, with the ortho maths untouched. bounds() reports the mesh footprint and forget() drops both readings of an edited file.
notes:
TILING READING CHOSEN (the file asked me to say which). Box and quad UVs are baked in METRES by measureUVsInMetres(), so all six faces of a box carry one texel density instead of stretching one rectangle over the lot. On top of that: a bare number is repeats per world unit (tiling: 2 on a 12 m wall gives 24 repeats), an array is absolute repeats across the box's front face or the quad (tiling: [2,1] gives exactly 2 across and 1 up). Defaults differ on purpose and are commented: a BOX with no tiling repeats once per metre (that is what "brick" means), a QUAD with no tiling shows its picture exactly once (that is what a decal, poster or sign is).

DECISIONS ANOTHER AGENT MAY NEED TO KNOW:
- entity.rotation on a mesh is applied about Y (yaw), in degrees, not about Z the way a sprite is. Tipping a wall over is never what a level meant. entity.scale multiplies solid geometry rather than setting it, since the geometry carries its own size.
- `mesh: "wall.png"` (the shorthand, no box or quad) takes its size from a THREE-number collider box if there is one, otherwise a 1x1x1 cube. So a wall can declare its size once, on the collider.
- Default sky is null and default fog is off, deliberately: setting either at construction would change how the existing 2D editor looks. Lights are always on, because MeshBasicMaterial ignores them so the 2D path cannot notice, and a 3D level that forgets its `world` block still has to be lit.
- setAmbient/setSun treat an omitted or null argument as "leave it alone" (an omitted sun direction no longer resets the direction — that was a real bug my harness caught). An unreadable colour, intensity or direction is reported with a [render] prefix and then ignored rather than applied as NaN.

SIGNATURE ADDITIONS (all additive, nothing existing changed):
- bounds(entity) now returns { w, h, d }; d is 0 for anything flat, so tool-transform's { w, h } destructuring is unaffected.
- toScreen(x, y, z = 0) takes an optional z, ignored by the flat camera. In perspective it also returns `behind: true` when the point is behind the eye, so a caller does not draw a gizmo at a convincing wrong place.
- toWorld(px, py) still returns { x, y } in ortho. In perspective it returns { x, y, z }: the first thing the ray hits, or the ground plane y=0 when it hits nothing, or 10 m along the ray if it is not pointing at the ground.
- renderer.camera is now a getter for the camera currently drawing, not a fixed property. renderer.scene is unchanged, which is what World Look's skybox sphere adds itself to; foreign objects in the scene are never removed by sync() and are never picked, both of which are correct.

COMPATIBILITY CHECKED against the other agents' landed work: plugins/builtin/world-look.js calls all four setters with exactly the argument shapes implemented, and its skybox radius (100) sits well inside my far plane (400).

VERIFICATION. `node bin/engine.mjs check` reports ok true and `node bin/engine.mjs --headless run tests.run` passes 8/8 (the five originals plus the three the other agents added). Neither exercises the renderer, since headless has no canvas, so I additionally drove the real makeRenderer in node with only THREE.WebGLRenderer stubbed — about 65 assertions covering camera selection, projection, ray picking (the wall in front, not the floor behind it), the ground-plane fallback, geometry sharing and rebuild-on-resize, material flags, both texture readings, forget(), all four setters, and the 2D path answering exactly as before. That harness lives at C:\Users\james\AppData\Local\Temp\render-harness\run.mjs. It is NOT checked in: I own only engine/render.js, and project/tests/ runs headless where there is no renderer to test. If someone wants renderer tests to survive, that needs a decision about where a browser-only test can live — worth raising as a painpoint.

summary: Wrote Physics 3D, the plugin that claims every entity whose collider box has three numbers, and added the reciprocal one-line guard to Physics 2D so the two plugins own disjoint sets of entities with nothing to configure. Movement resolves one axis at a time (X, then Z, then Y), sub-stepping whenever a body would travel further than its own smallest half extent, so a body slides along a wall instead of sticking and a 200 m/s body cannot pass through a 5 cm pane. Step height (default 0.46 m) lets a grounded body walk up a lip, and refuses when the body would not fit where it would arrive. It contributes context.raycast (slab test, nearest hit, axis-aligned face normal, ignore list and hit predicate, and no hit for a ray that starts inside a box) and context.canStand (the box grown about its feet), plus the commands physics3d.raycast — which takes [from, direction, maxDistance] or {from, to} with entity ids, so a sightline is one terminal call — and physics3d.bodies. Static solids are binned into a coarse X/Z grid rebuilt whenever one of them appears, moves or is resized. Contacts are reported once through world.hook on the step they begin, and a trigger body reports them while pushing nothing. project/tests/physics-3d.js covers all five required cases against project/levels/physics-3d-test.json.
notes:
CONTRACT SURFACE, live and verified from the terminal: context.raycast(origin, direction, maxDistance, options) and context.canStand(entity, height) are assigned in onLoad; origin/direction accept {x,y,z} or [x,y,z]. Defaults: properties.gravity -20.32, properties.stepHeight 0.46, both per-entity overridable.

DECISIONS ANOTHER AGENT SHOULD KNOW:
- Dynamic bodies block each other but never push each other. Deciding who yields needs a mass model this does not have; standing on another player still works, which is the Counter-Strike boost. A player-vs-player shove, if wanted, belongs in game code answering onCollide.
- Only solids push. Triggers report contacts and are never blockers (verified: a body falls straight through a trigger and still lands on the floor).
- The spatial grid bins solids by X and Z only, and rebuilds when a solid is added, removed, moved or resized — so a door that opens is noticed. castRay is deliberately linear over all 3D-collider entities and holds no state, which is what lets the test call it directly.
- physics-2d.js edit is exactly the `flat()` helper plus three filter guards. I confirmed empirically that a 3D body now receives gravity exactly once (fall position matches a single-gravity prediction to 1e-6), so the two plugins are not both claiming it.

FRICTION WORTH RECORDING AS A PAINPOINT (I did not run `engine pain` because painpoints.jsonl is not a file I was assigned, and concurrent agents append to it): the test API in plugins/builtin/tests.js hands a test `test` and never `context`, so nothing a plugin contributes onto context — raycast, canStand, camera.aim, input.look — can be reached from a test. I worked around it by exporting castRay as a pure named export from the plugin and importing it in project/tests/physics-3d.js with a comment saying why. A `test.context` or `test.run(commandId, args)` on makeT would remove the workaround for every plugin author. Cost roughly 6k tokens and 4 file reads.

GAP: the wiring of context.raycast/context.canStand is not covered by the test file, only the maths is. I verified the wiring by hand through `node bin/engine.mjs --headless run physics3d.raycast ...`, which goes through context.raycast, and through a throwaway node script for canStand (refuses 1.83 m under a vent, allows 0.91 m, allows 1.83 m in the open).

LEVEL NOTE: project/levels/physics-3d-test.json places everything as the existing `ground` type with a three-number collider on the placement, because three numbers is the only thing that makes an entity 3D and I was not allowed to create a type. Every placement carries an explicit id (floor, wall, low-ledge, high-ledge, faller, slider, stepper, climber) since they would otherwise all be ground-N. Bodies use the Counter-Strike box 0.81 x 1.83 x 0.81, so a rest height on the floor is 1.415.

summary: Wrote tools/make-counter-strike-textures.mjs, a dependency-free generator that paints 21 de_dust2 textures and writes them by hand as RGBA PNG with node's own zlib, following tools/make-sprites.mjs. Each texture is a base colour, a few octaves of periodic value noise for uneven sun, then the material's actual STRUCTURE drawn as geometry (recessed mortar with a light catch on every block arris, plank round-overs, panel rebates, pantile barrels, corrugation flanks), then a handful of large stains and cracks, then a small per-pixel grain last. Everything is generated on a torus: block grids divide the texture, staggered courses use even row counts, sinusoids complete whole cycles, and every draw helper wraps its coordinates. The tool checks its own work — it decodes each written file's IHDR back off disk to confirm the dimensions, bit depth and colour type, confirms both dimensions are powers of two, and measures a seam ratio per axis (the difference across the join over the sharpest line inside the texture), failing with a [make-counter-strike-textures] message and exit 1 if a join is more visible than the texture's own detail. Every axis that must tile scores under 1.0. It ends by printing a manifest: reference string, size, average colour, which axes tile, the measured seam, and a note. Seeds come from an FNV-1a hash of each texture's own name feeding a mulberry32 generator, so a re-run is byte-identical (verified by md5) and adding a texture later leaves the others untouched.
notes:
BUG IN ANOTHER AGENT'S FILES, needs fixing by whoever owns them: engine/ui.js assetURL resolves a bare name to project/assets/<name> and ANY name containing a slash to project/<name> as given. So these textures must be referenced as "assets/counter-strike/sand-floor.png". Three type files currently reference them without the assets/ prefix and will 404 at load (render.js will log "[render] missing texture /project/counter-strike/..."): project/types/brush.js:17 'counter-strike/sandstone-block.png', project/types/crate.js:13 'counter-strike/crate-wood.png', project/types/door.js:13 'counter-strike/door-blue.png'. I did not touch them — they are not mine. Either add the assets/ prefix in those three files, or change assetURL.

Average colours for picking a mesh tint, from the manifest: sand-floor #b29c74, sandstone-block #b6a17b, sandstone-brick #a78d66, plaster-wall #b9a687, plaster-trim #867458, crate-wood #9b7144, door-blue #41615b, door-metal #807b72, tarp-blue #436587, tunnel-wall #73644e, tunnel-floor #706048, stairs-stone #968566, roof-tile #a16240, ceiling-dark #4a4338, concrete #949189, rug-red #793e31, metal-panel #8d887f, sky #8fa0b2, decal-bullet-hole #938871, decal-blood #45100e, muzzle-flash #f9cc96.

Two deliberate deviations from "256 square or 128 square". plaster-trim is 256x64 — it is a band read from its paint edge down to the ground, not a repeat, so it TILES ON X ONLY; give it tiling [n, 1] and one tile of height. sky is 256x256 but also tiles on X only, because the gradient runs down it. Every other texture tiles both ways. The manifest's "tiles" column says which.

The seam metric has teeth, verified independently by decoding the written PNGs outside the tool: sky scores 54.3 on its (deliberately non-tiling) Y axis and plaster-trim 4.1 on its, against a 1.5 threshold, while everything that must tile scores 0.03 to 0.97. 2x2 montages of sandstone-block, sand-floor, plaster-wall, crate-wood and roof-tile were rendered and inspected — no visible grid.

Two design notes a level author may care about. A tiling wall cannot carry a single top-to-bottom gradient without seaming, so the grime a real wall has near the ground lives at the base of each course, and the wall base itself is what plaster-trim.png is for. The doors, the crate and the corrugated sheet put their frame, battens and bolt line ON the tile edge and weather by distance to that edge, so they still join to themselves when repeated — a wall of crates joins batten to batten.

RGBA is used for all 21 files (colour type 6); the three decals are the only ones with real transparency, and all three fade to alpha 0 well inside the quad. project/assets/counter-strike/ also contains models/ and sounds/ subdirectories from other agents; I only wrote the 21 PNGs at the top level of that folder and the one tool.

THE FOUR DECISIONS YOU ASKED ME TO STATE

1. Type registration: registered FROM THE PLUGIN, not a project/types/light.js. A light is an engine feature, and a type file would have to be copied into every project that ever wanted a lamp. The mechanism matters and is not obvious: `startWorld` boots plugins and THEN calls `loadTypes()`, which begins `world.types.clear()` — so a type registered in `onLoad` is wiped before the first level is read, and `loadTypes` is called as a local closure so it cannot be wrapped. The plugin therefore re-asserts on every `level:loaded` with `world.retype('light', LIGHT_TYPE)`, which both puts the definition back and heals every light the level has already spawned onto it (placement overrides survive, defaults fill in). The one real cost: `.engine/index.json` only indexes files under `project/`, so `light` does not appear in the Project panel and cannot be dragged into the viewport. Everything else works — `place.at` checks `world.types`, the inspector reads the definition off the entity, `snapshot` counts it. Painpoint p14 filed.

2. Shadow cap = 1, and it is a constant, not a setting. A shadow map is a second render of the whole scene from the light's view every frame; a point light costs six, because it renders a cube. On a map of several hundred boxes, one extra pass is already a large slice of 16 ms, and eight lamps quietly asks for nine renders per frame — which arrives as "the engine is slow" with nothing in the log. Off by default, opted in per light, over-cap refusals named on the console with their entity ids and why. A number you can raise is a number somebody raises.

3. Where the bake happens: NOT here, and it never will — stated in a comment above `resolveLightmaps`. Computing a lightmap is millions of rays plus denoising, minutes of a real renderer's time, and a browser tab attempting it would freeze the editor it runs inside. We drive a live Blender instance. What this file owes that baker is the manifest, and that is `lights.bake` — world-space metres, Y up, every static surface (id, type, position, rotation, size, texture, tiling, tint, target lightmap) and every static light, plus the level's ambient and sun read from World Look. Long surface lists are opt-in: `run lights.bake '{"surfaces":true}'`.

4. Ambient occlusion — SSAO, not vertex colours, and the route already exists. Another lane landed `plugins/builtin/post-processing.js` with an `ssao` effect declarable per level (`"post": [{ "ssao": { "radius": 0.4 } }]`), so nothing new needs building. Vertex colours cannot work in this engine and that is worth writing down: render.js caches BoxGeometry by size, so four hundred walls share one box — painting corners per wall means un-sharing that cache (megabytes of buffers and a load hitch, the exact thing the cache exists to prevent), and a box has eight vertices anyway, which cannot describe a corner gradient. Keep SSAO off by default like shadows, and off outright on any level with a lightmap, because the bake already contains that occlusion and doing both darkens every corner twice. I built neither, as instructed.

FOR THE RENDERER LANE — one thing I could not do from my side
`makeRenderer` never exposes the `THREE.WebGLRenderer` it wraps, so no plugin can set `renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true`. I set `castShadow` on the light and `castShadow`/`receiveShadow` on the scene meshes (only while a shadow-casting light exists, once per object), and three will still draw nothing. Rather than fail silently the plugin says so by name, once: "[Lights] this renderer does not expose shadowMap...". The fix is one line in render.js plus exposing it — painpoint p15 filed with that fix.
Also: `look(e)` in render.js does not include `e.mesh.lightmap`, so a lightmap applied after a mesh is built will not rebuild the material. I apply lightmaps at level load, before any mesh exists, so it works either way — but add `lightmap` to the `look()` key when you land it.

TWO THINGS I ACCEPTED, DELIBERATELY
- `mesh` is a placement key, so a level saved while lightmaps are applied writes the lightmap back onto each placement named. It is the same value the block already holds and the block is re-applied on every load, so it is idempotent and stable rather than wrong — but it is duplication. Blast radius reduced by only applying when something is drawing (headless never mutates, so CLI/test saves stay clean). Painpoint p16 filed.
- A light entity carries a small unlit marker box for the same reason spawn-point does, and the frame system hides it the moment the clock runs — which is the one line spawn-point's own comment asks somebody to write.

CONTRACT COMPLIANCE
Only my two files were created; nothing else was touched (three appends to painpoints.jsonl, which AGENTS.md asks for). No other lane's contribution is duplicated: no weapon table, no damage entry point, no second raycast. `context.lights.flash` has exactly the signature specified and accepts `at` as `[x,y,z]` or `{x,y,z}` so the weapons and effects lanes can hand it a raycast point directly. Names spelled out throughout, no wall clock, no Math.random, no setTimeout, four hooks respected (the type has none — a system is used, because `world.clear()` never fires `onDestroy` and a hook-based cleanup would leak a light on every level load).

summary:
Built two new engine plugins — Particles and Decals — that close the "particles" known gap, plus the test that proves them.

**plugins/builtin/particles.js** contributes `context.particles`:
- `burst({ at, to, count, direction, spread, speed, life, size, grow, colour, texture, gravity, fade, drag, blend, blocks })` — `to` spreads the particles along a segment, which is how a tracer is made from the same call as a puff. Colour may be a list, picked per particle.
- `trail(entity, options)` — returns `{ id, stop() }` and stops itself when the entity it follows is no longer the one the world holds under that id, so a trail on a spent grenade needs nobody to remember it.
- `blocked(from, to)` — segment-against-sphere over the clouds a `blocks:` burst declared. It lives here because smoke *is* the particles: the alternative is an invisible volume kept in step with the visible cloud by hand, and the moment those disagree somebody is hidden by smoke that is not on screen. It is answered against the declared cloud rather than the thousand particles because testing a segment against a thousand points for every bot every step is the loop that eats a frame budget.
- `effect(name, options)` over a table: muzzle-flash, tracer, brass, wall-hit, sparks, blood, smoke, flash, explosion.
- `recent(n)`, `state`, `clear`; commands `particles.recent`, `particles.state`, `particles.effect`, `particles.clear`.

Determinism: every direction, speed, life and size comes from `context.random` (a cone sample that costs the same two draws whether or not a direction was given, so option shape cannot shift the sequence) and steps on the fixed clock. Ceiling of 3000, oldest dropped, in one splice per burst rather than one shift per particle.

Drawing: camera-facing quads — four vertices sharing a centre, offset in *view* space in the vertex shader — in one buffer geometry per texture-and-blend. 910 particles measured as one draw call. Points were rejected because a point is clipped when its centre leaves the frustum, and a two-metre smoke puff pops out at the edge of the view.

**plugins/builtin/decals.js** contributes `context.decals.place({ at, normal, size, texture, life, tint, rotation })`, oriented by the surface normal and lifted 1 mm out of it (plus polygon offset) so a bullet hole never z-fights. Cap is 300 — Half-Life's own `r_decals` default — held in a ring, so the slot the cursor is about to write is by construction the oldest and recycling costs nothing. Merged into one buffer per texture, rebuilt only when a revision counter moves.

**The game glue** lives at the bottom of particles.js: it listens for `weapon:fired` (muzzle flash + brass ejected along direction×up, so a bot ejects a case the same way a player does), `weapon:hit` (tracer from the remembered muzzle, dust tinted by the surface texture + a rotated bullet hole, or blood + a splatter on the floor under the wound; a head shot sprays more), `entity:hurt`, `entity:killed`, and offers `grenade:detonated` and `bomb:exploded`. I read the weapon lane's real payload: on `weapon:hit`, `entity` is the shooter and `target` is what was hit — getting those round the wrong way would have put a bullet hole on the shooter.

Both degrade to nothing without a renderer: `three` is loaded by dynamic import on `shell:ready`, never at module scope, so a headless world does not pay to parse a 3D library it will never call — and the recording happens either way.

**project/tests/effects.js** covers all six things asked for: a burst records its count and is gone after its life (through the live fixed system, so a missing system registration fails it); the same seed puts all forty particles in the same place and a different seed does not; a decal sits 1 mm off the face `castRay` reported; 400 shots leave exactly 300 marks and it is the oldest hundred that went; a smoke cloud blocks a line through it, blocks one from inside it, and does not block one five metres beside it — and blocks nothing in the instant it lands, because the cloud opens out.
notes:
Verified: `node bin/engine.mjs check` → {"ok":true,"problems":[]}. `--headless run tests.run effects` → 1 passed. `--headless simulate 3 --level de_dust2` → "errors":[]. Every test that existed when I started (behaviour-attach, coin-pickup, de-dust-2, first-person-camera, gravity-lands, input-moves-player, jump, mouse-look, physics-3d) still passes.

Four tests in the final suite run fail — buy-menu, counter-strike-movement, materials, weapons. All four were written or last modified between one and six minutes before that run by other lanes still mid-write (weapons.js was 60 seconds old), the set of failures changed between consecutive runs as those files landed, and none of the four contains the string "particles" or "decals". They are not mine and are not regressions from this lane.

Two extra verifications I ran and then discarded (no files left behind, run via `node --input-type=module -e`):
1. Emitted the real payloads on the bus in a headless world and read back what came out — muzzle flash, brass, tracer, wall dust tinted #c9b489 from `sandstone-brick.png`, a bullet hole at 4.999 on a wall at 5.0 (the millimetre), and 26 blood particles plus a floor splatter for a head shot.
2. Stood in a real THREE.Scene for the renderer and stepped a frame: 910 particles and 2 decals came out as exactly two meshes, indexed, with draw ranges of 5460 and 12 — i.e. one draw call each, not 912.

One piece of friction worth recording as a painpoint (I did not write to painpoints.jsonl because it is not a file this lane owns, and a concurrent append during a nine-way fan-out could interleave): **a test is handed `test` and never `context`, so there is no way to reach a plugin's contributed surface from a test.** To exercise `context.particles` I had to import the plugin module and rely on module identity between the loader's import and the test's relative import, and to prove "the same seed gives the same smoke" I had to build a second `makeLoop` purely to get a re-seedable random stream, because `test` has no seed control. Cost roughly 6–8k tokens of design. A `test.context` (or just `test.seed(n)`) would have made both checks two lines. Kind: engine/cli; suggested fix: expose the context, or a `test.seed(n)` that calls `loop.reset`.

One judgement call worth flagging to the parent: the Counter-Strike-specific glue (the effect table, the surface-colour table, the bus listeners) sits at the bottom of particles.js. It belongs in a project plugin, but this lane owns only the two builtins and the test, and the brief explicitly required the listeners. It is in a clearly separated section with a comment saying that replacing the table makes it a different game's particle system rather than a different engine's — easy to lift out later.

summary:
Built two general engine features as plugins — a material library with a public registry and a custom-GLSL path, and a post-processing chain read from the level world block — plus a headless test for the parts that have logic in them. Nothing is named after Counter-Strike; the Counter-Strike look is one preset ("clean") among four.

MATERIALS (plugins/builtin/materials.js, plugin name "Materials")
Contributes context.materials.register(name, build), .list(), plus .get/.has/.resolve/.build and a materials.list command. Ships nine surfaces: basic, lambert (default), standard (metalness, roughness, normal and ambient-occlusion maps), phong, toon (adjustable steps via a nearest-filtered gradient strip, plus an optional rim outline), matcap, water, additive, and pulse — a whole material written from raw vertexShader/fragmentShader strings with a `time` uniform fed from context.time, registered through the same public call a game would use.

Declaration reading: every non-structural key on `mesh` is a parameter, and so are the keys inside `material: { name, ... }`, which win where they overlap. `unlit: true` still means `basic`, so existing sky faces and lamps draw unchanged.

Water animates from waterFlow(time, parameters) — a pure function of context.time, exported so it can be checked. A frame system (not fixed) pushes the clock into every animated material; materials remove themselves from that set on three's `dispose` event, so the set cannot grow for the life of the page.

Three is loaded only when `document` exists. A headless world imports no renderer library at all, and the registry, the declaration reading and the water flow all work with no screen — which is what the test exercises.

POST PROCESSING (plugins/builtin/post-processing.js, plugin name "Post Processing")
Reads `"world": { "post": [...] }` from the level, or a preset name. Effects: smaa, bloom, ssao, grade, vignette. Presets: none, clean (the almost-nothing one: SMAA, a whisper of bloom at threshold 0.95, a 2% warm grade), cinematic (heavy modern), retro (no AA at all, punchy contrast, hard vignette). Contributes context.post.set(chain) and a `post.chain` command that reads with no argument and sets with one.

An empty chain costs nothing, three ways, and the header says so: the plugin contributes NO systems at all (there is no per-frame work to skip), every pass module and three itself sit behind dynamic import() inside the build path, and renderer.passes.set is only called when there is something to set or something to tear down — so a renderer that has never been handed a pass never makes a composer or a render target.

TEST (project/tests/materials.js)
Registering a material makes it available by name; an unknown name falls back to lambert AND reports itself once, under the [Materials] prefix, naming the word that was wrong; parameters written flat and inside the material object both reach the builder while box/quad/model do not; the renderer's resolved texture and tint pass through untouched; waterFlow gives the same value twice for the same time, moves a second later, and normalises its direction. It states plainly in a comment and a test.note which part can only be checked in a browser.
notes:
VERIFICATION
- `node bin/engine.mjs check` → {"ok":true,"problems":[]}
- `node bin/engine.mjs --headless run tests.run` → my `materials` test passes (1/1 when run alone). Two tests fail in the full run and neither is mine, neither touches materials or post-processing, and both are other agents' in-flight lanes: `buy-menu` (weapons/buy lane) and `counter-strike-hud` (expects "AK47", HUD prints "AK-47"). `effects` and `lights` — which did not exist at the start of my run — now pass.
- `node bin/engine.mjs --headless simulate 3 --level de_dust2` → runs clean; the only console line is match-rules reporting warmup, from another lane.

ALIGNED WITH render.js MID-RUN
render.js landed its registries while I was working, so I read the real contract and rewrote my builders against it rather than my guess. Builders now take exactly what render.js hands its own two built-ins: `build({ mesh, texture, tint, view })`. I verified every one of the nine builders constructs a real three material against real three in node, with the exact request shape render.js sends (resolved texture with a repeat, a THREE.Color tint, the session view) — including that normal/matcap/AO maps inherit the main map's repeat so they tile with their albedo. I also verified the pass side: bloom, ssao, grade and vignette all construct, the grade uniforms carry through, and OutputPass constructs. SMAAPass could not be constructed in node (it needs Image) — browser only.

TWO THINGS THE NEXT AGENT SHOULD KNOW
1. There is one texture cache in this engine and it is render.js's. The main map comes from the renderer already resolved and tiled; only the SECOND maps a material needs (normal, matcap, ambient occlusion) are loaded in the plugin, because render.js resolves one texture per mesh. If render.js ever offers a texture helper to builders, that loader should go.
2. A limitation I documented but did not fix because the file is not mine: render.js's `materialLook` keys its shared-material cache on name, texture, tint and tiling — not on the material's own parameters. So two meshes that differ only in a parameter (two toons with different step counts) currently share the first one's material, and an object written at `mesh.material` stringifies to a name it does not have. Prefer the flat form (`material: 'toon', steps: 3`). Widening `materialLook` to include the resolved parameters is the fix, in engine/render.js.

WHERE THE COMPOSER LIVES
render.js owns the composer and puts a RenderPass at the front, but adds nothing at the back — so this plugin closes the chain with an OutputPass. Without it a composer's linear-light output reaches the canvas unencoded and every colour comes out washed. That is stated in the header, and the report notes why there is one more pass than effect.

NOT DONE ON PURPOSE
- No level was edited, so no level declares a `post` chain yet. de_dust2's right chain is `"post": "clean"` in its world block, one line, owned by whoever owns that file.
- I did not append to painpoints.jsonl. The real painpoint of this run — the material builder signature was unknowable until another agent's render.js landed, so I wrote against a guessed shape and rewrote the builder layer, roughly 12,000 tokens and 4 extra file reads — is worth recording, but painpoints.jsonl is not a file I was told I own and another agent already has it modified.

summary:
Built the damage lane: one entry point `context.damage(target, { amount, from, weapon, hitbox, direction, point })` in project/plugins/damage.js, the `damageable` behaviour that holds the numbers, and project/tests/damage.js proving all of it.

HITBOXES — a player is one box with no skeleton, so the body part is worked out from how high up the box the hit landed, measured from the feet: head above 1.55 m (x4.0), chest and arms 1.10–1.55 (x1.0), stomach 0.75–1.10 (x1.25), legs below 0.75 (x0.75). Measured from the feet and scaled onto a standing player by one multiplication, so a crouched 0.91 m box still has a head at the top of it and a standing body scales by exactly 1.0. Pass `point` from a raycast and the body part comes free; pass `hitbox` and it is taken as given.

ARMOUR — Half-Life's own formula, faithfully: `through = amount x armourPenetration`, `absorbed = (amount - through) x 0.5`, and when the plate cannot pay for everything it would have stopped it stops only what it can afford and the rest lands on flesh. That is what makes "I had armour and it did nothing" a true report of the last few points. Kevlar covers torso and arms; only a helmet covers the head; nothing covers the legs; a fall is never armoured. A helmet is good for exactly one head shot — which is why a Glock head shot (25 x 4 = 100, penetration 0.5) leaves 50 health and an AK head shot (36 x 4 = 144, penetration 0.775) kills through it.

DEATH — the entity is not destroyed. `damageable.alive` goes false (the field the movement, weapons, HUD and radar lanes already read), it drops its weapon through `context.weapons.drop`, plays a death sound, becomes `body: 'trigger'` so it blocks no doorway, and is flattened to 0.35 m and dropped onto the floor with one downward raycast — otherwise a standing corpse keeps stopping bullets at chest height for the rest of the round. `entity:killed` fires once, then `context.match.killed` if that lane is loaded. `context.damage.revive` is the other end of the round and stands the body back up out of the floor.

ALSO — fall damage above 7 m/s of downward impact, measured in the behaviour from the speed carried into the landing step (physics has already zeroed it by the time anything can look); `context.damage.blast(origin, ...)` with linear falloff and a raycast from the blast to each victim so walls stop it; `context.damage.flash(origin, ...)` which deals no damage and writes `blindUntil` / `blindAmount` scaled by distance and by how far off-axis the victim was looking, for the drawing lane to render.

VERIFICATION
- `node bin/engine.mjs check` → {"ok":true,"problems":[]}
- `node bin/engine.mjs --headless run tests.run damage` → 1 passed, 0 failed
- `node bin/engine.mjs --headless simulate 3 --level de_dust2` → runs clean, no [damage] or [damageable] output

Neither touches my three files, and both passed in the earlier 17/17 run. Every PRE-EXISTING test (behaviour-attach, coin-pickup, de-dust-2, first-person-camera, gravity-lands, input-moves-player, jump, mouse-look, physics-3d) passes.

WHAT THE TEST PROVES — 36 to the chest kills in three and 36 to the head kills in one (aimed with a point, so hitboxAt is exercised through the real path); kevlar halves a body shot and is worn down 91 from 100; five points of armour run out inside one hit and let 26 through, neither the 18 of full armour nor the 36 of none; a helmet saves a Glock head shot and not an AK one, and is consumed; a corpse is kept, stops being solid, lies on the floor, no longer intercepts a shot at chest height, and emits `entity:killed` once and not twice; a 4 m drop hurts and a 0.8 m drop does not; a grenade falls off with distance and does nothing through a wall; a flashbang blinds what could see it, does no damage, and wears off in the behaviour's own update.

CROSS-LANE NOTES FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR
1. project/plugins/weapons.js carries its OWN `hitboxAt` and its own `damageTo` armour arithmetic (its HITBOX table, ARMOUR_BONUS and falloff). Its live firing path does correctly call `context.damage(...)`, so the game applies damage once — but the table is a second copy of rules this lane owns, and the two already disagree: its head threshold is 0.88 of body height where the contract's 1.55/1.83 is 0.847, and it names a leg "leg" where the contract says "legs". I did not touch their file. I absorbed the naming half: `context.damage` now aliases leg → legs and arm/arms/body/torso → chest, because an unrecognised hitbox would silently cost a leg shot its 0.75 multiplier, which is the kind of wrong nobody notices and everybody feels. The threshold disagreement is still live and should be resolved by deleting their copy in favour of `context.damage.hitboxAt`.
2. The bag I declare matches what counter-strike-hud.js, radar.js, buy-menu.js and weapons.js already read: health, armour, helmet, team, alive, lastHurtBy. I added `lastHitbox` and `lastWeapon` because the HUD's kill feed reads `damageable.lastHitbox` to decide whether a kill was a head shot and nothing was writing it. The HUD's feed also depends on the victim surviving one step with `alive: false` — which is exactly what keeping the body gives it.
3. Every field is a declared behaviour property rather than state set in start(), so the generated index records the whole bag shape with its default values and another lane can read it without opening the file — and `alive` is never briefly undefined, which any `if (target.damageable.alive)` would read as dead.
4. `context.damage.revive(entity, { health, armour, helmet })` is the match lane's hook for the start of a round: it restores the collider, the body type, the standing height and a clean health bar. Bodies persist until it is called.

PAINPOINT RECORDED (p22, cli, ~6,000 tokens): a test is handed `test` and never `context`, so a test cannot call a plugin-contributed verb or subscribe to the bus. Two lanes in this run independently worked around it by exporting the live context from the plugin module and importing it back in the test. Suggested fix: add `test.context` (or `test.run(id, args)` and `test.on(event, fn)`) to makeT in plugins/builtin/tests.js.

summary: Built the weapons lane: a 29-weapon table with Counter-Strike's real numbers, the trigger (fire rate, ammunition, spray pattern, inaccuracy, wallbang), the carrying behaviour, and a test that proves all five contract requirements. check reports ok true, all nine baseline tests still pass, and de_dust2 simulates three seconds with no [weapons] errors.
notes:
WHAT OTHER LANES CAN CALL (all on context.weapons, all live — verified through `node bin/engine.mjs --headless run weapons.table`, 29 entries):
  table, get(id), give(entity, id, { select }), fire(entity), reload(entity), select(entity, slot), drop(entity)
plus four extras worth knowing about:
  prepare(entity)  — fills a carrier's running state; idempotent. Call it if you touch a bag before its first step.
  damageTo(id, { hitbox, distance, armour, helmet }) -> { health, armour }  — the armour/hitbox arithmetic. THE DAMAGE LANE SHOULD CALL THIS rather than reimplement it; the weapon's armourPenetration is the number that drives it and a second copy is how the AK stops one-shotting a helmet.
  falloff(id, distance), hitboxAt(target, pointY), slots, sprayResetSeconds
`slot` accepts 1-5 or the name: 1 primary, 2 secondary, 3 knife, 4 grenade (pressing again cycles), 5 bomb.

BUS EVENTS (drawing lane): "weapon:fired" { entity, weapon, origin, direction, ammo, shot }, "weapon:hit" { entity, weapon, target, hitbox, point, normal, distance, amount, penetrated }, "weapon:penetrated", "weapon:thrown", "weapon:dropped", "weapon:selected", "weapon:reloaded".

THE BAG: filed under BOTH entity['carries-weapons'] (the engine's own name, from the file name) and entity.carriesWeapons (the name the contract gave the other eight lanes). Both point at one object. It carries the contract shape plus moveSpeedFactor (the plain number the movement code reads — AWP 0.84, AK 0.884, knife 1, Scout 1.04), magazines/reserves (per-weapon, so a switch does not hand out a fresh magazine), lastShotAt, recoilPitch/recoilYaw.

RECOIL, the one design decision worth flagging: the pattern is a POSITION the aim must be at on shot n, not a per-shot nudge, so what is punched is (pattern[n] − camera.punchPitch). Game Camera's recovery constant is 0.09 s, which is far faster than Counter-Strike's; kicking by the per-shot delta instead lets the aim settle two degrees up and stay there — a spray that never walks. The bullet leaves along the aim BEFORE this shot's kick lands, which is why the first bullet of a burst is accurate and tapping works. Bots get the identical numbers through entity.aimYaw/aimPitch when the camera is not following them; there is no private path.

CROSS-LANE NOTES:
- weapon.name is spelled properly — "AK-47", "M4A1 Carbine", "Desert Eagle". The HUD reads it via context.weapons.get(id).name and its test now agrees.
- give() on an entity with no "carries-weapons" behaviour is refused by name on the console. project/plugins/buy-menu.js line ~381 builds a stand-in bag `{ grenades: [] }` when entity.carriesWeapons is missing — prepare() will adopt and fill that object rather than crash, but an entity with no behaviour gets no reload completion and no speed factor. The two player types already attach the behaviour correctly.

- Where a number was a judgement rather than a known value (accurate ranges, reload/deploy tenths, recoil climb and sway for weapons other than the AK) the comment says so and the value preserves the ordering between weapons.
- Missing sounds are noted in the table where they bite: no P228, shotgun, TMP or M249 report exists in the set, so those borrow the nearest thing and say which.

summary: Built the movement lane: counter-strike-movement (the Quake/HL/CS move in metres, driven only by wish fields), player-controlled (keyboard and mouse turned into those fields), the terrorist and counter-terrorist body types, and a test that pins the feel. check is ok, my test passes, de_dust2 simulates clean.
notes:
WHAT IS THERE

project/behaviours/counter-strike-movement.js — the model, and nothing else. Reads entity.wishForward, wishStrafe, wishJump, wishCrouch, wishWalk and aimYaw; writes velocityX/Y/Z, entity.crouched (the field the camera already drops the eye on), entity.moveSpeed (what the sound lane reads) and a halved collider box while ducked. Ground: friction first, then Quake's accelerate. Air: the same accelerate with the reachable speed clamped to 0.76 m/s while the acceleration term keeps the full wish speed — faithful to PM_AirAccelerate, and the reason air-strafing pays. Jump is the RISING EDGE of wishJump ("don't pogo stick"), and friction is skipped on the step you jump, which is what lets a chain of hops keep its speed. Crouch replaces the collider rather than editing it (the object may be the type's own) and grows about the feet; standing up asks context.canStand and is retried every step until it is allowed.

project/behaviours/player-controlled.js — the only file in the lane that knows a human is present. Edges are detected in its own bag rather than through input.pressed(), because `pressed` is cleared once a FRAME while this runs once a fixed STEP and one frame can carry five steps: a semi-automatic pistol would have fired five times per click.

project/types/terrorist.js and counter-terrorist.js — 0.81 x 1.83 x 0.81 dynamic bodies, mesh pointing at the GLBs with a collider-sized tinted box as the fallback the renderer draws until a model loader exists, properties.team spelled out, behaviours [counter-strike-movement, carries-weapons, damageable], and start() gives glock18 / usp through context.weapons.give (guarded, reports once by name).

summary: Fixed all five confirmed defects in engine/render.js plus the texture warning storm, then added GLB model loading with posable named nodes, a second-pass viewmodel layer, the materials and passes hook points, lightmaps on a second UV set, and static geometry merging with a render.stats readout. `node bin/engine.mjs check` reports ok true and `--headless simulate 3 --level de_dust2` runs clean with no errors; render.js is not in the headless import graph (only engine/index.js imports it), so nothing here can affect the headless suite.
notes:
TEST STATUS — read this before assigning follow-up work.

`node bin/engine.mjs --headless run tests.run` ends 16 passed / 2 failed: `bots` and `counter-strike-hud`. Neither can involve my change, and here is the proof rather than an assertion: `grep -rln "render.js" engine bin plugins project` finds exactly one importer, `engine/index.js`, which is the browser entry. `engine/start-world-node.mjs` imports only files.js, start-world.js and project-index.mjs. The headless world never loads the file I edited.

The failure set also moved three times while I worked — `buy-menu` failed, then passed, then failed, then passed again; `counter-strike-hud` failed with two different messages — because eight agents are writing `project/` concurrently. `buy-menu` failed on `test.entities` returning nothing while `simulate` proved de_dust2 does have spawn-points for both teams, i.e. a reader in another lane mid-edit.

THE FIVE DEFECTS

1. render.js:44 `texture()` — the onFail callback is now kept in a per-file state table with a waiting list, so the fortieth wall referencing a missing file falls back to the visible per-type tint exactly like the first. Callers also consult `statusOf(src, mode)` before building, so an already-failed file never even reaches the texture path.
2. `m.material.transparent = opacity < 1` now goes through `setOpacity()`, which sets `needsUpdate` — and only when the flag actually changed, since `transparent` is in three's program cache key and recompiling every frame is its own bug.
3. `behind` is now a camera-space test: `point.clone().applyMatrix4(camera.matrixWorldInverse).z > 0`, computed before `project()` mutates the vector. The old `p.z > 1` called a point 400 m ahead "behind" and a point genuinely behind but in range "in front".
4. `mesh: "wall.png"` is normalised once in `meshOf()`, so the size path and the material path read the same object. The shorthand now actually textures.
5. `number()` reports through `report()` with a `[render]` prefix. It only complains about a value that was written down and cannot be read — an absent size is answered by the documented, deliberately visible metre cube. `report()` de-duplicates because geometry is read every frame.

THE WARNING STORM
`Texture.clone()` shares the original's `Source` but flags the copy for upload immediately (three r169 Texture.copy line 139). With no image yet, WebGLTextures.setTexture2D:513 warns once per copy per frame. Fixed two ways: `guardUpload()` holds a copy at `version = 0` until the shared Source has an image, and textures are now cached by resolved repeat, which turns ~233 copies on de_dust2 into ~8.

WHAT A BROWSER MUST SHOW FOR THIS TO BE RIGHT — I cannot test a renderer headless, so this is the checklist.

1. NO REGRESSION. de_dust2 in 3D looks exactly as it did: brush textures at the same density on every face, crates and doors in place. `level1` in 2D unchanged — sprites, sheet frames, `flip`, painter ordering by z then list position.
2. CLEAN CONSOLE. Zero "THREE.WebGLRenderer: Texture marked for update but no image data found". This is the single easiest thing to check and the most likely to regress.
3. THE MERGE, MEASURED. `engine.eval('engine.context.renderer.stats')` about a second after de_dust2 loads. Expect `drawCalls` down from roughly 260 to roughly 80-100, `merged` near 200 of ~290 entities across ~22 batches. I measured the grouping offline against the level file: at a 32 m cell, 22 material groups of 4+ cover 200 entities. If `merged` is 0, the settle counter is not advancing; if `drawCalls` did not drop, the batches are not being drawn.
4. MERGE EVICTION — THE RISKIEST PART. Drag a wall in the 3D viewport. It must leave its batch on the frame its transform changes, with no ghost left at the old position, and the batch must rebuild the same frame. Then let go and wait ~0.75 s: it rejoins. Clicking a merged wall must still select it — merged entities keep an unrendered mesh on layer 1 that only the raycaster looks at.
5. MODELS. Terrorists and CTs draw as GLB models rather than tinted boxes. Setting `entity.pose = { legLeft: -0.4, legRight: 0.4, torso: 0.1 }` rotates those nodes about X. I verified against the files: terrorist.glb exports legLeft, legRight, armLeft, armRight, head, weaponMount, torso, hips, root, with no skin — which is exactly why a hinge per node is the whole feature and no animation system is needed.
6. MODEL FAILURE. Point a type at a .glb that does not exist: a tinted box, and one `[render] missing model ...` line naming the file.
7. VIEWMODEL. `renderer.viewmodel.set({ model: 'counter-strike/models/ak47.glb', position: { x: 0.16, y: -0.16, z: -0.42 } })`, then walk into a wall. The rifle must not clip. `renderer.viewmodel.offset({ x: 0.01 }, { y: 0.02 })` moves it. Calling `set` with the same model every frame must not stutter — it is treated as a move, not a swap.
8. OPACITY. `entity.opacity = 0.5` on a brush actually dims it now (the editor's hover preview), and the entity drops out of its batch while dimmed.

THINGS I FOUND IN SIBLING LANES AND HONOURED
- `plugins/builtin/materials.js` states in its own header: "Widening `materialLook` in engine/render.js to include the material's own parameters is the fix; that file belongs to the renderer, not to this plugin." Done — the material key now includes every non-structural key of the declaration, so two toons with different step counts no longer share one material. It also reads `material: { name, ...parameters }`, so `materialNameFor` reads both the string and the object form the same way that plugin does.
- `plugins/builtin/post-processing.js` expects the renderer to own the RenderPass at the front and to take an ordered list after it. That is what `passes.set` does. The composer and both example modules are behind a dynamic import, so an empty list allocates nothing.
- `project/types/terrorist.js` declares `box` beside `model` as the deliberate fallback, so `meshShape` prefers a declared box over the collider for a model.
- `plugins/builtin/lights.js:630` reports by name that "render.js needs `renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true` and to expose it". I did both (PCFSoftShadowMap) and merged batches copy castShadow/receiveShadow from their members. This is outside my written job but inside my file, and it removes a standing false report from another lane; shadows cost nothing until a light sets castShadow.

DELIBERATE TRADE-OFFS WORTH KNOWING
- I merged rather than instanced. Instancing was the wrong axis here and I checked before choosing: only 41 of 281 entities on de_dust2 share a size with seven others, because every wall is its own size. Merging by material catches 200. Batches are cut by a 32 m grid cell as well as by material, or one merged geometry spanning the map would have one bounding sphere and could never be frustum-culled — buying draw calls by selling culling.
- Frustum culling was already on (three culls per object by default). What I added is keeping it useful after the merge, and turning it off for the viewmodel, which must never be culled.
- A lightmap on generated box geometry gets a per-face 0..1 second UV set, so one image stretches across each face. A proper atlas needs per-face offsets, which is a level's business. A model brings whatever uv1 its file declared.
- I did not touch ARCHITECTURE.md (its kernel line-count table is stale for render.js), per the instruction not to write documentation.

summary:
Built the round, the bomb and the money for the Counter-Strike clone: project/plugins/match-rules.js (the rules and the economy), project/types/bomb.js (the planted C4, which owns its own fuse and its accelerating beep), and project/tests/match-rules.js (all six required proofs, on de_dust2).

The plugin contributes context.match.{state, phase, money, pay, killed, hold/plant/defuse, bomb} and the commands match.state, match.skip and match.round — all three of which work from a cold headless call because they start the match out of warmup themselves. context.match.state and context.world.state.match are the same object under two names, so the HUD, an agent running "hud.read", and a test all read one number rather than three copies of it.

Rules implemented exactly as specified: freeze 6 s, buy 15 s from round start, round 1:55, fuse 35 s, defuse 10 s / 5 s with a kit, 10 s between rounds, first to 16, sides swap after 15. Win conditions are checked in the contract's order, and the two that are easy to get wrong are right: the round does NOT end on the timer when the bomb is down, and killing the last terrorist after the plant does NOT end it either. Economy: 800 start, 16000 ceiling, 3250 a win, the 1400/1900/2400/2900/3400 ladder that resets on a win, 800 to the planter, 300 to the defuser, and the per-weapon kill table with the knife at 1500 and the AWP at 100 (the weapons table's own killReward overrides it if it declares one).

Integration with the eight other lanes: it reads entity.wishUse — the field player-controlled and bot-brain already write — so planting and defusing have exactly one door and a bot has no private path. It calls context.damage.revive, context.damage.blast, context.weapons.give and context.match.killed's caller (damage.js) through the declared contracts, every one of them guarded for absence. It publishes entity.frozen, entity.money and entity.hasBomb as plain fields, reads entity.hasDefuseKit for the buy lane, and picks "you" with the identical four-step ladder the HUD and radar use so the screen cannot show one player's health beside another's wallet.

Verified: "check" reports ok true; the match-rules test passes; every test that passed before still passes. The one red test in the suite is "bots", which belongs to another lane, fails identically with my plugin removed, and whose failure messages change run to run because that agent is editing it live.
notes:
Decisions worth knowing about:

1. Freeze time is enforced, not announced. Nothing else reads entity.frozen yet — counter-strike-movement does not — so the plugin declares needs: ['Physics 3D'] and pins every combatant back to its spawn anchor after physics has run in the same fixed step. A lane that starts reading entity.frozen changes nothing; a lane that never does still cannot walk out of spawn.

2. A combatant is anything with a damageable bag or a carries-weapons bag, deliberately not "anything typed player". Something with no damageable bag can never die, and one unkillable body on a side would make that side impossible to eliminate — a round that can never end for a reason nothing on screen explains.

3. A match only starts on a level that has spawn points or bomb sites AND a combatant on each side. Otherwise it stays in warmup and says so once, by name, on the console. This is what keeps level1 and physics-3d-test untouched.

4. Death is noticed two ways: damage.js calls context.match.killed (the contract), and every live step the plugin also looks for a body that has gone alive:false without anyone saying so, using damageable.lastHurtBy for the kill reward. Both go through one idempotent path, so a death nobody announced still ends the round and still pays.

5. The bomb type owns going off; the round writes bomb.explodesAt when it spawns it and reads bomb.exploded back. One clock, one actor — and a bomb dropped into a level by hand still counts down with the plugin absent.

6. The planted bomb spawns with the fixed id "bomb-planted", so an agent can read it by name.

7. Two things I did that touch the edge of my lane, both guarded and both commented: the plugin binds 'use' to KeyE only if nothing has bound that action yet (nothing had, so planting was otherwise unreachable by a human), and it passes the current armour into damage.revive so kevlar survives the round that bought it, which is 1.6's behaviour and the damage lane's default would have thrown away.

Cross-lane friction the parent may want to route: the "bots" test simulates ten seconds from spawn on de_dust2 and now spends the first six of them in freeze time. bot-brain already reads context.match?.phase === 'freeze', so the lane knows about it, but their test's ten-second budget probably wants to start after freeze (state.match.freezeEndsAt can be pulled in, exactly as match.skip does). That test was already failing before this lane landed, so nothing is blocked on it.

Reporting into world.state is done every fixed step rather than once, because a type's start hook may assign context.world.state = {...} wholesale — the demo player does — and a match that reported itself once would vanish the first time a level did that.

summary:
Built the Counter-Strike 1.6 HUD, the rotating radar and their test. Three new files, nothing else touched.

**project/plugins/counter-strike-hud.js** — "Counter-Strike HUD". Split in two on purpose: a FIXED system reads the world into one plain `reading` and advances every animation on the fixed clock; a FRAME system draws that reading and computes nothing. That is what makes the whole HUD testable with no screen. It repaints every frame (stated in the header comment with the reason: the crosshair gap, bob, sway, recoil, kill-feed fade and muzzle flash all change on essentially every frame, so a change-detection key would cost a JSON stringify per frame and save nothing) but skips the paint wholesale when the game is not running or the level is not a Counter-Strike one.

Draws: health cross + number and armour shield + number bottom left (health flashes red on the way down only), money in green above them (flashes on change), weapon name over "magazine / reserve" bottom right, round clock with both scores and alive counts top centre, kill feed top right fading over five seconds and coloured by team, crosshair centre, a red timer panel plus a blinking C4 icon when the bomb is planted, a "You were killed by X" band with spectator hand-off on death, and a flashbang whiteout (the damage lane leaves `blindUntil`/`blindAmount` explicitly for "whatever draws").

Crosshair: four rectangles and a gap that is the sum of movement, airborne, spray (`carriesWeapons.shotsFired`) and an optional `entity.inaccuracy`, tightened while `entity.crouched`, and eased toward the target rather than snapped.

Viewmodel: drawn in 2D. `engine/render.js` has one scene and one camera and offers no viewmodel layer, so the header says plainly that the 3D upgrade is a second scene with its own near plane and that swapping in the GLB is a change to `drawViewmodel` alone. The motion is all there and all on the fixed clock — figure-of-eight bob scaled by ground speed, sway that lags the view and catches up, a recoil kick fired off the carrying bag's own `lastShotAt`, a lower-and-raise on weapon switch, a reload driven by `reloadStartedAt`/`reloadingUntil` so the animation and the ammunition cannot disagree, and a procedural muzzle flash lasting exactly three frames. Six silhouettes chosen by the weapons table's own `slot`.

**project/plugins/radar.js** — "Radar". Dark rounded square top left, clipped, rotating so up is the way you face. The outline is derived from the level's solid boxes once per level load (268 shapes on de_dust2) and drawn through one canvas transform in world metres, banded into floor / low cover / wall by height relative to your feet — so standing in the tunnels does not show you the courtyard. Team dots with facing ticks, off-radar mates clamped to the rim, a ring on whoever carries the C4, a diamond for the planted bomb (the entity, or the named site when only the match lane knows). Enemies appear only when a living team mate has range, a 150-degree cone and a clear `context.raycast` — recomputed ten times a second, not sixty.

**project/tests/counter-strike-hud.js** — asserts on the data, never on pixels. Both plugins export a `running…()` handle for it, the same singleton-module trick `plugins/builtin/camera.js` uses. Covers: `hud.read` reporting health, armour, "AK-47 24 / 60", money with a dollar sign and the round timer counted down from the match's deadline; the same numbers in `world.state`; the crosshair gap opening while moving and closing again; the kill feed gaining a line on a `damageable.alive` transition (with killer and headshot read from `lastHurtBy`/`lastHitbox`) and losing it after the fade; and the radar showing a team mate, hiding an enemy sixty metres off, showing one three metres ahead, and losing it again when you turn your back.

VERIFIED

- `node bin/engine.mjs --headless run tests.run` → 19 passed, 0 failed (including the new counter-strike-hud test)
