Neither plugin was ever disabled by the loader, so the browser-only paint path has no reference errors.

THE 3D VIEWMODEL IS THE UPGRADE. I read engine/render.js: one GL context, one scene, one camera, no viewmodel pass. The gun is therefore a 2D silhouette in the HUD canvas with the motion done properly. The right fix is a second scene with its own camera and near plane composited over the world — every offset drawWiewmodel uses is already in metres and radians, so it is a change to that one function.

CONTRACT POINTS WORTH FLAGGING TO THE OTHER LANES
1. The contract says `entity.carriesWeapons`, but the engine files a behaviour's bag under its file name — `entity['carries-weapons']`. carries-weapons.js aliases the two in its `start`, so both work once started. Both my plugins read either name, so they are correct before it starts too.
2. Nobody publishes a weapon inaccuracy on the entity — weapons.js keeps `coneOf` private. My crosshair reproduces the same four states from plain fields (velocity, `crouched`, `grounded`, `shotsFired`) and will pick up a 0-to-1 `entity.inaccuracy` the moment the weapons lane writes one, with no change here.
3. `hud.read` reads the built-in HUD's item list, not a canvas, so the Counter-Strike HUD registers its lines there and switches the built-in PAINTER off while it is drawing (one line, reported once on the console per level). One set of numbers, two consumers — otherwise the same six numbers get drawn twice in two places.
4. One writer per world.state key. `match-rules` owns `scoreTerrorist`, `scoreCounterTerrorist`, `phase`, `money`, `aliveTerrorist`, `aliveCounterTerrorist` and `bombPlanted`; the HUD reads those and writes them only when no match plugin exists. The HUD owns `health`, `armour`, `helmet`, `alive`, `weaponName`, `magazine`, `reserve`, `ammunition`, `roundClock`, `roundSeconds`, `blinded`, `killedBy`, `crosshairGap`, `killFeed`, `team`; the radar owns `radarDots`, `radarEnemies`, `radarBomb`.
5. `match-rules` picks whose money to publish from `context.camera.target`, and the HUD picks whose HUD to draw the same way. If the camera's level rule has not resolved yet the two can disagree for a few frames (my test points the camera by hand for exactly this reason). Worth knowing if anyone sees one player's health beside another's wallet at level load.
6. The kill feed is built by watching `damageable.alive` fall over rather than by a kill event — no new contract, works with or without match-rules. The one thing it cannot see is a victim destroyed outright rather than marked dead; a body needs to survive one step with `alive: false` on it.

NOT FAILING, BUT NOTED
- `project/types/player.js` still does `context.world.state = {...}` wholesale in `start`. Harmless here because the HUD writes its keys onto whatever object is current each step, but it will silently wipe another lane's state if that lane writes once and never again.
- Two commands added for agents: `counter-strike-hud.read` and `radar.read`. Both say "the world has not been stepped yet" rather than returning nothing when called on an unsimulated world, because a bare `run` never steps the loop.

summary: Built the bot lane: a navigation plugin that samples the walkable surface off de_dust2's own geometry and runs A* over it, a readable state-machine brain that drives a player body through exactly the wish/aim fields a human's player-controlled writes, and a test that proves routes, sightlines, reaction time and that a bot actually walks somewhere.
notes:
RECAST: `recast-navigation` is NOT in package.json and NOT in node_modules, and nothing was installed. The grid is hand-rolled. Recast would be the upgrade — a real navmesh with polygons instead of a 0.5 m lattice, smoother paths and no per-column height limit. The seam for it is the exported `buildNavigation(entities)` in bot-navigation.js: swap what it returns and neither the plugin surface nor the brain notices.

NAVIGATION (project/plugins/bot-navigation.js, contributes context.navigation.path/walkable/nearest/regionAt/stats, plus commands `navigation.stats`, `navigation.path`, `navigation.bots`):
23,667 columns at 0.5 m, 8,900 walkable, 30 regions, built in ~150 ms of work reported as deterministic counters (73,932 ground probes, 28,296 box tests) rather than a wall clock, which game code cannot reach.
Two decisions were not obvious and both were found by the map coming out in forty pieces:
- The walkable surface for a column is the LOWEST one with headroom, not the highest. Taking the highest puts the floor on top of every awning, lintel and door sill in de_dust2 and deletes the doorway underneath. Standing on a crate still works, because the floor inside a crate has no headroom and fails first.
- The clearance test ignores anything whose top is within one step height (0.46 m) of the surface, because that is what a step height means — Physics 3D walks a body up onto it. Without this every staircase in the map reads as a wall: a 0.5 m tread is narrower than a player, so from any tread the next one up overlaps the footprint.
Rebuilds are lazy and guarded: `world:changed` only marks it stale, and the next query compares a few hundred solid positions before deciding to resample — otherwise a spawned tracer would cost more than every bot on the map.

MAP BUG FOR THE LEVEL LANE: `navigation.stats` reports a 188-cell island of walkable floor at [-28.95, 1.3, 15.05] with no route to the rest of the map — a 1.3 m ledge with no steps, higher than a 0.77 m jump apex. Drives the body only through `wishForward`, `wishStrafe`, `wishJump`, `wishCrouch`, `wishWalk`, `wishUse` (+ `useHeld`, which match-rules reads under that name) and `aimYaw`/`aimPitch`/`rotation` — the same fields `player-controlled` writes off the keyboard and camera, consumed by the same `counter-strike-movement`. Human feel: reaction time 0.5→0.2 s by skill with a ±30% roll, started only when a target enters the cone AND a ray reaches it; 90° cone, staggered so ten bots never spend their rays on the same step (one pass does sight and hearing together); aim that turns at 4→11 rad/s with a 1.15 overshoot and an error that decays as exp(-tracked/0.6); bursts of 5→2 at range and a held trigger inside 8 m; stops moving past 12 m to shoot. Hearing is read off plain fields (an enemy whose `nextShotAt` is in the future is loud at 45 m, one running at 18 m, one walking is silent) because the audio plugin records sounds without a position.
Two bugs worth naming: holding jump when stuck is a trap — an airborne body accelerates at 0.76 m/s so a stuck bot bunny-hops into the same wall forever (stuck counts hit 58 in a soak); it is now a tap plus a 0.45 s sidestep, and soak counts sit at 0–2. THE SPLIT (kernel vocabulary, plugin policy — stated in a comment in both files)
- engine/shell.js gained `shell.focus(on)` / `shell.focused` / `shell.root`. focus() toggles a `focused` class on the `.app` frame and calls `renderer.resize()`, because the viewport just changed size and no window resize event says so — the camera aspect comes from the viewport, so a renderer left on the old size draws the world stretched. Nothing is removed and draw() is not called: hidden is recoverable, rebuilt is not.
- engine/style.css: `.app.focused` collapses the grid to `0 1fr 0 0`, hides the docks and the status line, and flattens the toolbar to a zero-height overflowing strip holding only the play/STOP button plus a fading ESC hint. Plus `#app:fullscreen`.
- plugins/builtin/play-focus.js ("Play Focus") owns when: `play:started` -> focus(true) + requestFullscreen, `play:stopped` -> focus(false) + exitFullscreen.

THE GESTURE. `editor.togglePlay` emits `play:started` synchronously from the play button's own onclick, so the listener is still inside the user gesture and real fullscreen is granted. Starting play from a terminal is not a gesture; the request is refused and it says so by name once, in engine.errors(), naming what to press instead. Verified live: "[play-focus] the browser refused full screen (Permissions check failed)... press PLAY in the toolbar rather than starting play from a terminal, or press FOCUS...". Deduped by kind because a browser answers one refusal twice (rejected promise + fullscreenerror); `why` always carries the latest and `play.focus` reports it.

WHAT ESCAPE MEANS (written down at the top of the plugin and returned by the command). Counter-Strike's answer: first press gives the mouse back and the round carries on — that is the menu; second press leaves full screen, `fullscreenchange` fires and the docks come back, still playing; only STOP stops play. The way out is always visible: the STOP button floats at (10,8), the bar itself takes no pointer events so a shot at the top of the screen is still a shot.

COMMANDS: `play.focus` reports { focused, wanted, fullscreen, screen, playing, why, escape }; `play.focus true|false` sets it by hand. Plus a FOCUS toolbar button, which is the real-click route back into fullscreen after Escape or after play was started from a terminal.
